findings.title: UniPoolerCutoverCore routes the whole protocol LP through the OWNER EOA across separate broadcast txs (step 4 withdrawBPT -> step 5 exit -> step 6 seed) with simulation-baked bptIn/sAmt/pAmt and no resume path; any Balancer swap between simulation and the exit strands the liquidity on the EOA
findings.rootCause: Non-atomic EOA custody of the cutover liquidity (steps 4-6 are independent OWNER txs whose amounts are fixed in forge simulation) combined with no skip-if-done resume gates. The escrow (UniPoolerCutoverEscrow.exitAndSeed) that removes this is not wired into the core at a4f9f3c.

findings.variantDecision: Scenario B kept in this finding (same root cause). Both scenarios end with protocol value on the OWNER EOA mid-sequence and no resume; the defect enabling both is step 4 moving BPT to the EOA in a separate tx with no idempotent gates. One mitigation (atomic escrow exitAndSeed, or core resume gates + floor-based seeding) closes both. B differs only in which leg of the stall holds the value (BPT vs pool tokens).
findings.description: Under forge --broadcast, steps 4, 5 and 6 are separate OWNER transactions whose amounts are baked in simulation. A Balancer swap that lands before the step-5 exit either (A) shifts the per-BPT composition inside the 1% _checkMinAmountsOut window so the exit succeeds but the baked step-6 addLiquidity pulls more of the short leg than OWNER holds (0 spare sUSDS, 1.47 phUSD), or (B) pushes the exit past its floor so it reverts after step 4 already moved all BPT to OWNER. Either way ~$41.3k of protocol POL sits on the OWNER EOA, which story 103's 2026-10-07 requirement ('no protocol funds transit the owner EOA') forbids. The canonical pair stays empty and public, which extends the ledgered 2-wei poisoning window (9a694ae01fe1), and index 4/hook remain on the old pooler. Re-running the core fails at step 5 (bptIn == 0) or step 0.
findings.economicAnalysis: ECON-001: zero extractable value. The seed either lands at exactly the simulation price or the short-leg transferFrom reverts, so the core can never seed at a manipulated ratio. The attacker's round trip loses ~2 x 0.3% fee (-0.60 sUSDS at 100, -1.11 at 185.7, -11.2 at 2,000). Pure grief at <$0.20/attempt. The 1% tolerance (~$206.6/leg) is a revert bound, not a loss bound (refutes MR-002's 'up to 1% extractable').
findings.impact: Liveness + custody: protocol liquidity stranded on an EOA until a hand-written recovery; new pair left exposed to the 2-wei poisoning brick meanwhile. No third-party theft path (owner controls the EOA, Law 3).
findings.attackVector: Organic: the pool saw 5 swaps in the last ~7 days. Adversarial: watch the mempool for OWNER's removeLiquidityProportional and front-run it with a dust swap in either direction. This is the same ~$0.03 trigger as ycn L-28. Here the exit SUCCEEDS (it stays inside the floors) and the seed reverts. Under a --slow Ledger broadcast forge then halts. State: ~18,572 sUSDS + ~22,559 phUSD (live share of 20,401.8 BPT) sit on the OWNER EOA, which is exactly what story 103's 2026-10-07 'no funds through any EOA' requirement forbids. UniPoolerV2 is deployed but unseeded, the canonical pair exists and is empty and public (poisonable, see 9a694ae01fe1), and index 4/hook are still on the old pooler. There is no resume entry point: re-running _runCutover fails step 5 (bptIn == 0, L374). Without --slow, steps 7-12 would still land after the failed seed and cut index 4 over to an UNSEEDED pooler.
findings.recommendation: Wire story 103 onto UniPoolerCutoverEscrow.exitAndSeed (atomic, whole-balance seed). Until then, do not broadcast the core in PROPORTIONAL mode. If it is kept, seed desired = the on-chain-guaranteed minAmountsOut floors (not simulation deltas), sweep the remainder later, and add per-step skip-if-done gates.

findings.title: UniswapHelper add-liquidity guard is existence-only, so an honest user can become first LP of the empty canonical sUSDS/phUSD pair and permanently brick both the cutover core (step 2) and UniPoolerCutoverEscrow (PairNotEmpty); story-109's stated safety rationale is not achieved
findings.rootCause: _requirePair() reverts only when getPair == 0, not when reserves are (0,0); story 109/111 treat 'pair does not exist' as the safety boundary, but createPair is permissionless and cutover step 1 creates the pair in its own tx before step 6 seeds it.

instances.note: runbook premise 'pair does not exist until Stage 4'

findings.description: The helper gates liquidity on the canonical pair EXISTING, not on it having reserves. Story 111 deploys the helper BEFORE the cutover. The pair exists from cutover step 1 onward, and earlier if anyone calls the permissionless factory.createPair. Any addLiquidity through the helper while the pair is still empty makes that caller the first LP and gives the pair non-zero reserves. That permanently fails core step 2 (L339/344) and the escrow's PairNotEmpty, and UniPoolerV2's canonical-pair constructor check means no alternative pair can be used. The deploy script's NatSpec (DeployUniswapHelperMainnet.s.sol L43-46) presents 'pair does not exist' as the safety boundary. That boundary does not cover the step-1..step-6 window or a pre-created pair.

storyFaithfulness.summary: Letter of story 109 satisfied (blocks pair creation through the helper); its stated purpose (prevent seeding before 103's cutover) is not. Law 1 overrides: the spec ships an honest-user path to the 9a694ae01fe1 brick.

findings.attackVector: Unlike the ledgered attacker poisoning, this can be triggered by an honest user or a UI build that exposes the add-liquidity form once the pair address resolves. The helper resolves it live via getPair, independent of the PhusdSusdsPair address-book key.
findings.impact: Bricks the Balancexit cutover design (core step 2 and escrow PairNotEmpty); MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY lock means reserves can never return to 0; UniPoolerV2 canonical-pair constructor forbids an alternative pair; first LP sets the price. Liveness, no direct theft.
findings.recommendation: Revert in the helper's add paths when either reserve is 0 (EmptyPair) so the helper can never be the first LP. Correct runbook/story-111 wording: the pair may exist before Stage 4.

findings.title: Cutover core's 'read live' rescue amounts and post-conditions (mintDebt==0, old pooler drained, _assertRetired) run only in forge simulation; interim index-4 mints before step 10 leave unswept sUSDS on the paused old pooler, and a re-enabled donation could revert the step-11 USDS rescue
findings.rootCause: ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast: amounts read in simulation are baked into calldata; every require between external calls is simulation-only, while index 4 still dispatches to the old pooler until step 10 is mined.
findings.description: The 'read live after step 10' amounts are read in simulation and baked into the rescue calldata. The drain checks at L532-535 and in _assertRetired run only in simulation. Until the step-10 tx is mined, index 4 still dispatches to the old pooler, and every interim mint wraps USDS into sUSDS ON the old pooler (BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch). That sUSDS is not covered by the baked rescue. It stays on the old pooler after step 12 pauses it. The mint rate since the 2026-10-01 holding pattern is ~1,957 sUSDS in ~12 days. Conditional brick: if the owner re-enables the donation on the old pooler before the cutover (live batchDonationSize is 0, so this does NOT apply to today's config), an interim mint's PSM sweep consumes the parked USDS. The on-chain balance can then fall below the baked usdsRescued, so the step-11 USDS rescue reverts. The broadcast halts before step 12, leaving the old pooler unpaused with NFTMinterV2 still its minter. PATTERN-003 adds: the step-7 mintDebt==0 check and the step-4/5/6 baked bal/bptIn/sAmt/pAmt are the same simulation-only mechanism (the step-5/6 facet is carried by DEDUP-001 and not double-counted here).
findings.attackVector: None. Ordinary index-4 mints during the multi-tx broadcast window.
findings.impact: No loss: rescueERC20 is onlyOwner and not pause-gated, so residue is recoverable (opportunity cost per ECON Q4). Retired pooler silently keeps protocol sUSDS that in-script post-conditions claim is zero; conditional step-11 revert (only if donation re-enabled; live batchDonationSize = 0) halts before step 12.
findings.recommendation: Run step-11 rescue in a second invocation after step 10 is mined, or have story 103's verify assert old-pooler sUSDS/USDS == 0 and mintDebt == 0 live after broadcast and sweep residue.

findings.title: Index-4 mints revert OnlyDispatcher for the ~11-tx window between cutover step 8 (hook.setDispatcher) and step 10 (replaceDispatcher), and the core has no resume gates, so a halt inside the window leaves index 4 bricked
findings.rootCause: Step 9's new-pooler setters sit between the hook repoint and the dispatcher swap, and the core has no skip-if-done gates (step 0 requires hook.dispatcher == oldPooler).
findings.description: After step 8's setDispatcher lands, BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.onDispatch reverts OnlyDispatcher for the old pooler (hook L109-110). ATokenDispatcherV2.dispatch calls hook.onDispatch unconditionally, so every index-4 mint reverts until step 10 is mined. In between sit setHook plus the step-9 setters: setMinter, setPSM, setMaxTout, setBatchMinter, setBatchDonationSize, setAuthorizedPooler x4 and setNudgeStreamer, about 11 Ledger-signed --slow transactions. The window is inherent to three independent owner contracts. The real hazard is that the core is not resumable. If the broadcast halts anywhere in steps 8-10 (Ledger timeout, gas, nonce), index 4 stays bricked, and re-running _runCutover fails step 0 L297 (hook.dispatcher != oldPooler). Story 103 says 'resume from receipts', but the core has no skip-if-done gates to resume through.
findings.impact: Index-4 mints revert (user keeps USDS, loses gas; no fund loss per ECON Q4) for the window, indefinitely if the run halts inside it.
findings.recommendation: Move step 9's configuration before step 8 (it touches only the new pooler) so steps 8-10 are three consecutive transactions. Give story 103 per-step idempotent gates (as StableStakerCutoverCore did after L-02 2c82d65e65e1), or disable index 4 in NFTMinterV2 across the window.

findings.title: RECOVERY exit branch never enables Balancer V3 Recovery Mode; MockBalancerVault conflates 'paused' with 'recovery allowed', so test_cutover_recovery proves a property false on mainnet and the plan's 'step 5 already allows for that' fallback does not hold
findings.rootCause: Mock (story 100 spec) models paused => recovery; on mainnet Recovery Mode is a separate state requiring Vault.enableRecoveryMode(pool), which neither the core, the story, nor the planned fork approach calls.
findings.description: On mainnet, a Balancer V3 pool being paused does not put it in Recovery Mode. Someone must call the permissionless Vault.enableRecoveryMode(pool) first. Live today: isPoolInRecoveryMode = false. The core's RECOVERY branch never calls it. MockBalancerVault conflates the two states (poolPaused => recovery allowed, L243), so test_cutover_recovery 'proves' a property that does not hold on mainnet. The DeployMocks rehearsal (PROPORTIONAL only) does not exercise it either. The yield-claim-nft escrow fork test does call enableRecoveryMode explicitly (UniPoolerCutoverEscrow.fork.t.sol L216).

storyFaithfulness.obligationFor: story-103: add 'if !vault.isPoolInRecoveryMode(pool) then vault.enableRecoveryMode(pool)' before the RECOVERY exit (or a step-0 require), and make fork case 2 use the real enableRecoveryMode rather than a mocked pause query.

findings.impact: Fail-closed liveness at the deadline-pressured moment (after 30 Oct): RECOVERY_EXIT=true reverts PoolNotInRecoveryMode unless an operator enables recovery mode first.
findings.recommendation: In the RECOVERY branch (or as a step-0 precondition) call vault.enableRecoveryMode(pool) when !isPoolInRecoveryMode(pool); model recovery mode independently in MockBalancerVault; story-103 fork case 2 must use the real enableRecoveryMode, not a mocked pause query.
findings.fixNuance: Fork: enableRecoveryMode reverts SenderNotAllowed() 0x23dada53 for a stranger AND for OWNER while the pool is live. The suggested fix only works once the pool/vault is actually paused (the post-30-Oct scenario); the paused-pool path was NOT tested (pause state not reproducible on fork). Plan says Balancer will enable Recovery Mode 'where needed', which may moot it.

findings.title: UniswapHelper's hardcoded DOLA venue (Curve DOLA-3CRV) is near-empty: the DOLA route caps at ~$1.5k USDC out (-69% at 5k DOLA), and story 109 required a fork depth check for USDe but not DOLA
findings.rootCause: Venue selection: CURVE_DOLA_3CRV holds ~1,889 DOLA / ~1,488 3CRV at block 26181407; story-109 depth-check gap let it ship.
findings.description: The address and indices are correct (coins(0)=DOLA, 3pool coins(1)=USDC, so underlying index 2 = USDC). But at block 26181407 the pool holds only ~1,889 DOLA and ~1,488 3CRV. get_dy_underlying returns: 100 DOLA -> 99.62 USDC; 10,000 USDC -> 1,888.7 DOLA (-81%). Every DOLA leg crosses this pool with a 0 intermediate minimum. Only the caller's final minOut protects them. ECON-003 depth curve: DOLA->USDC 1,000->984.95 (-1.5%), 2,000->1,519 (-24%), 5,000->1,543 (-69%); USDC->DOLA 2,000->1,818 (-9%). Quote path uses the same pool, so quote-derived minOut protects users; the trap is a UI that shows output without price impact. Story 109 L168 asks for USDe depth only; L241 records a ~0.002% optimistic bias on USDC->DOLA (zero-tolerance minOut reverts, fail-closed).

storyFaithfulness.summary: No DOLA depth check in the story; spec gap.

findings.impact: DOLA route effectively unusable above small sizes; user value at risk only with minOut==0 or a UI without price-impact warning. Leak goes to Curve LPs/arbitrageurs, not from protocol funds.
findings.recommendation: Pick a deep DOLA venue before the story-111 broadcast (plan L186: DOLA/sUSDS Curve), or have the UI compute and block on price impact versus pair spot for every route.

findings.title: Story-103 rewire respec turns a self-healing condition into a griefable DoS: dropping the step-2 skim makes a 1-wei unsynced pair donation fail simulation, and the current _assertRetired owner-BPT==0 require must be removed or a 1-wei BPT donation to OWNER griefs the run
findings.rootCause: Story 103 checklist (L202) specifies step 2 as assert reserves AND balances (0,0) with no skim, whereas escrow.exitAndSeed would harmlessly skim exactly that donation; _assertRetired L552-553 conflicts with the 2026-10-10 'must not revert on non-zero owner BPT' amendment.
findings.description: Story 103 (incomplete, checklist L202) has step 2 DROP the skim and 'only assert the pair is empty (reserves AND balances (0,0))'. With the skim gone, a 1-wei UNSYNCED transfer to the pair fails the simulation at step 2. Yet escrow.exitAndSeed would harmlessly skim exactly that donation to newPooler (escrow L365-366). The spec turns a self-healing condition into a griefable DoS. Separately, the current core's _assertRetired (L552-553) requires owner BPT == 0. Story 103 (L203) correctly says the rewired core must NOT revert on non-zero owner BPT. That require has to be removed in the rewire, or a 1-wei BPT donation to OWNER before simulation becomes a grief.
findings.impact: Liveness only, marginal (an attacker can already sync -- the 9a694ae01fe1 brick).
findings.recommendation: In the rewire, assert reserves == (0,0) only and leave balances to the escrow's skim. Drop the owner-BPT clause from _assertRetired.

evidence.notes: Spec-level; story 103 implementation not in tree at a4f9f3c.

findings.title: Story 103 contradicts itself: its Background cutover sequence (L59-71) and step-0 precondition (L150), plus BalancerWinddownPlan.md Stage 2, still prescribe the superseded OWNER-EOA custody flow that the 2026-10-07 / 2026-10-10 amendments forbid
findings.rootCause: Amendments appended without marking the superseded sections; source plan not updated.
findings.description: The same story's Background 'Cutover sequence' (L59-71) still gives the superseded EOA flow: step 2 `withdrawBPT(OWNER, fullBalance)`; step 3 'Exit the OWNER's whole BPT balance'; step 4 'addLiquidity ... from the owner; this creates the pair'; step 9 'USDS dust sweep'. Technical Details L150 still has the step-0 'pair absence or (0,0) reserves' precondition. The source plan Stage 2 (docs/BalancerWinddownPlan.md:376-428) also still prescribes OWNER custody: `skim(OWNER)`, `withdrawBPT(OWNER, fullBalance)`, parked USDS 'rescueERC20(USDS, OWNER, fullBalance)', and the griefing-recovery text 'the recovered sUSDS and phUSD sit on OWNER'. The landed core (story 100, which predates the requirement) implements exactly that flow: UniPoolerCutoverCore.sol:341, :362, :373, :425-430, :521. The authoritative incomplete story contradicts itself, and its named source plan contradicts its latest requirement. An executor reading top-down meets the EOA flow first. The commit/plan text claims an order and a custody model that the story no longer asks for.
findings.impact: No Law-1 exploit: EOA custody by a trusted owner is not an attack path. The value at stake is the accounting and tax provability the human asked for, plus the risk that 103 ships an un-rewired core.
findings.recommendation: Before 103 executes, mark Background L59-71 and L150 as superseded by the 2026-10-07/10-10 amendments (as story 100 L52 did), and add an escrow-flow note to plan §4 Stage 2.

findings.title: Cross-project numbers refresh (NOT a new finding): plan section 5 / Stage 4 seed-price and crossing figures are stale -- live seed price 0.916 USDS/phUSD (plan 0.971), live crossing Delta* 1,895 USDS (plan ~$640, F-03-052 $1,712); errs safe
findings.rootCause: Price drift since plan block 26,093,540 (holding pattern stopped pool() 2026-10-01).
findings.description: The seed price carried over by the proportional exit is 0.8233 sUSDS = $0.9160 per phUSD. For a 50/50 weighted pool, the token-unit balance ratio equals the spot price, so the V2 seed reproduces the Balancer spot exactly, as plan decision 3 intends. The seed is 8.4% below the $1 mint price. Minting is mint-only (no redemption floor), so a below-peg seed opens NO mint/sell arbitrage. Back-running the seed has no edge either: the V2 pair and the Balancer remnant start at the identical price. Since the plan's block 26,093,540, the price has fallen from 0.971 to 0.916 (the holding pattern stopped pool() on 2026-10-01). The live crossing Delta* on the seeded pair is 1,895 USDS, against the plan's ~$640 and F-03-052's $1,712. Using the stale figure for the 'first call about Delta*' errs SAFE (undershoot, no arb skim). Pooling the whole post-cutover sUSDS balance at once (1,957.66 sUSDS = 2,178 USDS) overshoots by ~$283, lifts phUSD to ~$1.0125, and costs about $0.2 of arb skim (~141 phUSD minted, which is collateral the no-ceiling design wants).
